title: Limitations on damages: editorial notes and questions
summary: Read the surrounding notes and questions alongside the principal cases. The complete assigned pages are preserved here.
notes:
Rockingham County v. Luten Bridge Co.: Luten Bridge introduces mitigation as a limit on recovery. It also distinguishes the wrongfulness of repudiation from the injured party’s response to it.

Parker v. Twentieth Century-Fox Film Corp.: Parker shows that mitigation protects an employee’s substantial nonmonetary interests as well as pay. Its procedural disagreement also warns against treating every difference between two jobs as automatically decisive.

Hadley v. Baxendale: Hadley supplies the organizing distinction between ordinary and special consequential loss. It also illustrates why factual notice and the procedural treatment of that notice matter as much as the verbal rule.

Kenford Co. v. County of Erie: Kenford makes it necessary to ask what risk the defendant assumed, rather than infer responsibility from bare knowledge of possible gain. It belongs beside Hadley and the contrasting Article 2 discussion.

Fera v. Village Plaza, Inc.: Fera contrasts with Kenford’s unsuccessful profit claims and clarifies what reasonable certainty requires. It also separates sufficiency of evidence from appellate disagreement with a jury’s choice.
